def: Evolution in which a candidate's fitness depends on other populations that are evolving at the same time.
Co-evolution in which populations are rivals, such as solvers against test cases built to break them.
Co-evolution in which each population supplies one part of a solution and members are scored by how well they work together.
The pattern where all sides keep adapting to each other and none pulls ahead, so a flat score hides continuing change.
Training many models in parallel while copying strong workers over weak ones and perturbing hyperparameters during the run.
Replacing a poorly performing worker's weights and hyperparameters with a copy of a better worker's.
Perturbing copied hyperparameters, for example by multiplying the learning rate by 0.8 or 1.25, before training continues.
A setting such as the learning rate that changes over the course of training instead of staying fixed.
Deciding which part of a team or sequence deserves the credit or blame for the overall result.
